extracted.intended_audience: general readers; young men and early-career professionals seeking practical career, management, and public-speaking advice (as presented in an autobiography)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted practical principles and standards for personal development, public speaking, management, and early-career advancement drawn from an autobiographical chapter (Andrew Carnegie).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public speaking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: “My two rules for speaking then (and now) were: Make yourself perfectly at home before your audience, and simply talk to them, not at them. Do not try to be somebody else; be your own self and talk, never 'orate' until you can't help it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice emphasizes conversational delivery, authenticity, and composure before an audience; avoid grandiose oratory unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join debating/literary societies to build confidence and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: “I know of no better mode of benefiting a youth than joining such a club as this. Much of my reading became such as had a bearing on forthcoming debates and that gave clearness and fixity to my ideas. The self-possession I afterwards came to have before an audience may very safely be attributed to the experience of the 'Webster Society.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in small debating/literary clubs trains reading choices, sharpens ideas, and develops self-possession for public speaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use operational work as a school for composition and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: “The operating-room of a telegraph office is an excellent school for a young man. He there has to do with pencil and paper, with composition and invention.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, routine technical work can cultivate writing, composition, and inventive problem-solving skills valuable beyond the specific job.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire broad knowledge (esp. current/foreign affairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Knowledge is sure to prove useful in one way or another. It always tells. ... My slight knowledge of British and European affairs soon stood me in good stead.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad reading and topical knowledge create opportunities and can distinguish an operator/employee; cultivate general knowledge beyond narrow job tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: When filling gaps (making guesses), be cautious and conservative
rubrics_metrics.description: “My guessing powers were said to be phenomenal, and it was my favorite diversion to fill up gaps instead of interrupting the sender ... This was not a dangerous practice in regard to foreign news ... My guesses were quite safe, if I got the first letter or two right.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compelled to infer missing information, rely on conservative cues (first letters, context) to avoid introducing significant errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master rare technical skills to stand out
rubrics_metrics.description: “I finally became an operator by sound, discarding printing entirely. The accomplishment was then so rare that people visited the office to be satisfied of the extraordinary feat. This brought me into such notice ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing uncommon or highly-valued technical abilities can attract attention from superiors and create advancement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek opportunities beyond assigned duties to gain exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: “The battle of life is already half won by the young man who is brought personally in contact with high officials; and the great aim of every boy should be to do something beyond the sphere of his duties—something which attracts the attention of those over him.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively take on responsibilities or tasks outside your formal role to gain visibility with decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle entrusted responsibility with utmost care (trustworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative of losing and recovering the pay-roll package: the author notes that had he lost it permanently, he would have lost essential confidence and possibly his career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability in safeguarding important items or information is critical; a single lapse can have long-term career consequences—maintain rigorous care and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management: prefer gentleness and light, certain punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: “Only experience teaches the supreme force of gentleness. Light but certain punishment, when necessary, is most effective. Severe punishments are not needed and a judicious pardon, for the first offense at least, is often best of all.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a manager, favor proportionate, consistent discipline and mercy for first offenses; experience tempers initial strictness and suggests leniency is often wiser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women as reliable telegraph operators (hiring recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our experience was that young women operators were more to be relied upon than young men. Among all the new occupations invaded by women I do not know of any better suited for them than that of telegraph operator.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to recruit and train young women as telegraph operators based on observed reliability and suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept social invitations from superiors to build rapport
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdotes where invitations (tea, Sunday visits) from superiors (Mr. Lombaert, Mr. Stokes) were described as honors and led to closer relations and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating in social engagements with senior figures can enhance personal recognition and lead to mentorship or career openings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save early and invest; pool small investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of first investment: mortgage house to borrow $500 to buy shares; 'It gave me the first penny of revenue from capital ... We resolved to save and to watch for the next opportunity for investment in which all of us should share.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start saving and investing early, even small amounts; consider cooperative/pooled investments with peers to increase opportunity and learning about capital income.
